summary: This memo creates the first official IANA registry entries for permanent mail and MIME header fields, following the registration procedure of RFC 3864. It lists the standard header names, such as those used in email messages, in one place so that new headers do not clash with existing ones.

eli5.summary: Email messages have labelled lines at the top, like From and Subject. This document writes down an official list of those labels so nobody invents the same label for two different things.

questions: what are the registered email header fields
what is the permanent message header field registry
what is the difference between sender and from header
subtitle: The first official IANA list of permanent mail and MIME header fields, from Date and Subject to Content-Type.

tldr.problem: Mail and MIME messages carry many named header fields, and without one authoritative list two people could use the same name for different things.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4021 supplies the initial registrations of 75 mail header fields and 13 MIME header fields, each as a template giving description, protocol, status, controller and specification, following the procedure in RFC 3864.
tldr.outcome: The registrations seed the Permanent Message Header Field Registry. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 5322.

today: RFC 4021 is a Proposed Standard and is updated by RFC 5322. It has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: What This Document Registers
sections.content:
RFC 4021 gives the initial IANA registrations for a number of mail message and MIME header fields, using the registration procedures for message header fields in RFC 3864. It contains no new protocol. Its main body is automatically generated from RDF/N3 data.

Section 2.1 holds the templates for mail header fields and section 2.2 holds the templates for MIME header fields. Most of the information comes from Jacob Palme's earlier work in RFC 2076 and later updates.
sections.eli5: It is a phone book for email labels. It does not invent new labels, it just writes down the ones already in use.

sections.title: The Registration Template
sections.content:
Each header field gets a template with the same few entries: a Description, the Applicable protocol (Mail or MIME), a Status, the Author/change controller, the Specification document(s) and Related information. In every entry the controller is the IETF, with the IESG mailbox as contact.

The status values used are standard (23 entries), standards-track (57), obsolete (6), experimental (1) and work-in-progress (1). Each section also opens with a summary table of header names, so you can scan the list before the full templates.
sections.eli5: Each label gets an index card with the same blanks: what it means, who owns it, and whether it is still in good standing.

sections.title: Core Mail Header Fields
sections.content:
The mail section covers 75 fields. The best known are marked standard and point to RFC 2822, with the note that they were defined as standard by RFC 822. These include Date, From (the author's mailbox), Sender (the agent that actually transmitted the message), Reply-To, To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, Comments and Keywords.

Threading and tracing fields sit alongside them. Message-ID is a single unique identifier for a particular version of a message, and it is kept if the message is resent without changes. In-Reply-To and References name related messages, and RFC 2822 changed References to list the Message-IDs of the preceding reply chain. Received carries trace information from each mail transfer agent, and Return-Path carries the return path. The Resent-* family covers messages that are reintroduced into the transfer system.
sections.eli5: These are the labels every email has: who wrote it, who it is for, what it is about, and when. Others record each stop the message made on its trip.

sections.title: Mailing List, Notification and Specialised Fields
sections.content:
Many mail fields serve narrower jobs. The List-* group (List-Archive, List-Help, List-ID, List-Owner, List-Post, List-Subscribe and List-Unsubscribe) lets a mailing list identify itself and point at its archive, help, posting and subscription addresses. Disposition-Notification-To and Disposition-Notification-Options relate to disposition notifications, and Importance is a hint about how important a message is, with values high, normal or low, and it is not used to control transmission speed.

A large block of fields comes from mapping between X.400 and Internet mail, mostly from RFC 2156 (MIXER). Examples are Autosubmitted, Autoforwarded, Incomplete-Copy and the X400-* fields. Their entries are marked as for MIXER and not for general use. Some fields are marked obsolete: Obsoletes was renamed Supersedes by RFC 2156, and Encrypted is also listed as obsolete.
sections.eli5: Some labels are for special jobs, like telling you how to leave a club's mailing list, or marking a letter that came from a different kind of post office.

sections.title: MIME Header Fields
sections.content:
The MIME section registers 13 fields. MIME-Version says a message follows MIME and which version. Content-Type gives the format of the content, Content-Transfer-Encoding gives the coding method used in a body part, and Content-ID and Content-Description identify and describe a part, for example a caption for an image. All of these point to RFC 2045.

Others deal with where and how a part is shown. Content-Disposition says whether a part is shown inline or is an attachment and can suggest a filename. Content-Language carries a language code such as en. Content-Location gives a URI for the body part, Content-MD5 carries a checksum of the content, and Content-Duration gives a duration in seconds. Content-Base was in the first version of MHTML but was removed in the second, and Content-Alternative is marked work-in-progress.
sections.eli5: These labels describe what is inside the envelope: a picture, a sound or plain words, how it was packed, and whether to show it right away or save it as a file.

sections.title: IANA and Security Considerations
sections.content:
The IANA Considerations say that section 2 provides the initial registrations in the "Permanent Message Header Field Registry" defined by the procedures in RFC 3864.

The Security Considerations are short: no security considerations are introduced beyond those already inherent in the use of the referenced mail message header fields.
sections.eli5: The list is handed to the official record keeper. Writing the list down does not add any new danger to email.
